beliefs: f strips the first character when the input starts with an uppercase letter followed by a lowercase letter (any lowercase letter works) [E6]
f also strips the first character when the uppercase letter is followed by a digit, space, or symbol, as long as the string has length ≥2 [E2, E6]
f does NOT strip when the uppercase letter is followed by another uppercase letter (e.g. 'AB', 'HELLO') [E2, E3]
Two-character strings starting with uppercase followed by lowercase are returned unchanged [E3, E4]
Single uppercase letters are returned unchanged [E2, E4]
Strings of length ≥3 starting with uppercase+lowercase are stripped [E1, E4]
Strings starting with lowercase, digit, space, or empty are returned unchanged [E1]
The rule appears to be: strip first char if length ≥3 and first char is uppercase and second char is NOT uppercase [E2, E3, E4, E6]?
notes: E6 shows stripping happens for any lowercase letter after the uppercase, and also for digit/space/symbol after uppercase when length≥3 (E2 'A1'→'1', 'A '→' '). E3 shows two-char strings are never stripped. So the rule is: length≥3, first char uppercase, second char not uppercase.
